# Wovely, every public page

> Wovely (wovely.app) is a crochet pattern organizer with a row counter and stitch tracker, made by Wovely, LLC in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida. Free for five patterns; Craft is 6.99 USD a month or 54.99 USD a year. Each entry below is one page, in the page's own words.

## Wovely: Crochet Pattern Organizer and Row Counter App
URL: https://wovely.app/
Summary: Save every crochet pattern, track every row, and keep your projects in one place. The home for your hooks, yarn, and works in progress.
H1: More making. Less managing.

What it does: import a crochet pattern from a PDF, photos, a link or pasted text and keep the original in the Vault; BevCheck verifies every row's stitch counts before the first stitch; your place is kept row by row on every device; multi-part patterns and MCAL collections get a clue calendar; gauge, yardage and scale calculators; yarn and hook stash with supply lists.

Pricing, as the page shows it: Free for 5 patterns with full row tracking and BevCheck on every import, no card. Craft is 6.99 USD a month or 54.99 USD a year for up to 100 patterns, advanced imports, collections, the Vault, calculators, full BevCheck and live chat that reaches a real person. Through November 30, 2026 the code COZY takes half off Craft for the first three months.

## Crochet Yardage, Gauge and Scale Calculators | Wovely
URL: https://wovely.app/tools
Summary: Free crochet calculators, no signup: yarn yardage, a gauge swatch turned into real stitch counts, and a pattern scaled up or down without redoing the math.
H1: Crochet gauge, yardage and scale calculators

Each calculator also has its own page, with the questions people actually ask about it: the gauge calculator, the yarn yardage calculator, and the pattern scale calculator.

Gauge. Crochet a square, measure four inches across the middle of it rather than at the edges, and count the stitches and rows inside that measurement. Put those numbers in with your target size and you get the number of stitches to start with and the number of rows to work. Measuring the edges is the usual reason a blanket comes out the wrong width.

## UK to US Crochet Terms Converter, Whole Pattern | Wovely
URL: https://wovely.app/uk-us-crochet-terms
Summary: Convert a whole crochet pattern between UK and US terms in one pass. dc, tr, htr and dtr are handled together so shared names cannot collide. Free, no signup.
H1: UK to US crochet term converter

The two dialects do not use different abbreviations. They use the same abbreviations for different stitches. UK dc is US sc. US dc is UK tr. That overlap is the whole problem.

Work down a UK pattern with a chart and you change every dc to sc. Then you reach a tr and change it to dc. Your pattern now contains two kinds of dc: the ones you already converted and the ones you just created. Go back over it and you convert the new ones a second time. One pass, done by a person, quietly corrupts the document.

## Crochet Abbreviations: sc2tog, fpdc, Magic Ring | Wovely
URL: https://wovely.app/crochet-abbreviations
Summary: Every common crochet abbreviation with its UK equivalent and a plain note on how the stitch is worked. Paste a row you are stuck on and each term gets labeled.
H1: Crochet abbreviations, explained

Single crochet two together, a decrease. Pull up a loop in the next stitch, then pull up a loop in the one after, so you have three loops on the hook. Yarn over and pull through all three. Two stitches have become one and your count drops by one.

The mechanics are the same: several partly worked stitches closed together at the top. The difference is where they go. A dc2tog is worked across two different stitches and decreases your count. A cluster is usually worked into one stitch or one chain space, so the count does not drop and you get a solid textured bump instead.

## Crochet Gauge Calculator: Swatch to Stitch Count | Wovely
URL: https://wovely.app/crochet-gauge-calculator
Summary: Turn a crochet gauge swatch into real numbers: your stitches and rows over a measured swatch, the finished size you want, and the counts to start with. Free.
H1: Crochet gauge calculator

Work a square a good deal bigger than the area you plan to measure, in the stitch the pattern uses, then lay it flat without stretching it. Measure a four inch window somewhere in the middle rather than at the edges, and count the stitches and rows inside it. The edges of a swatch always lie about the tension.

Hook size first, because it moves tension the most for the least effort. A larger hook gives you fewer stitches to the inch, a smaller hook gives you more. Change one size, work a fresh swatch and measure again. If the stitch count comes right and the row count is still off, that is normal in crochet and usually handled by working to a measurement rather than to a row number.

## Crochet Yarn Yardage Calculator: How Much Yarn? | Wovely
URL: https://wovely.app/yarn-yardage-calculator
Summary: Estimate the yards a crochet project needs from its finished size, yarn weight and stitch. Single and double crochet are not the same answer. Free, no signup.
H1: Yarn yardage calculator

It depends on three things and nothing else: the finished area, the yarn weight and the stitch. A worsted weight throw around 50 by 60 inches in single crochet runs well over a thousand yards, and the same blanket in double crochet uses noticeably less, because taller stitches cover more area per yard. Put your own numbers in above rather than trusting a rounded figure from a blog.

A single crochet is short and dense, so it takes many more stitches to cover the same square inch. Double and treble crochet are taller and more open. Same yarn, same blanket, and the yardage can differ by a third or more purely on stitch choice.

## Crochet Pattern Scale Calculator: Resize to Gauge | Wovely
URL: https://wovely.app/crochet-pattern-scale-calculator
Summary: Resize a crochet pattern to a different finished size or to your own gauge, keeping the stitch counts a whole multiple of the repeat so the round still closes.
H1: Crochet pattern scale calculator

For a plain fabric, largely yes. For anything with a repeat, no: the new count has to stay a multiple of the repeat or the pattern stops lining up at the end of the round. That is why this page takes the repeat as well as the count and rounds to a number that still works.

Two ways, and they are not equivalent. A heavier yarn with a bigger hook keeps every stitch count identical and scales the whole thing, which is the safe route. Adding increase rounds changes the shape as well as the size, and for a piece that has to be stuffed and sewn, shape changes compound.

## Crochet Stitch Counter: Does This Round Add Up? | Wovely
URL: https://wovely.app/crochet-stitch-counter
Summary: Paste a written crochet round and see how many stitches it makes and how many it works across. When the two numbers differ, you know which round to recount.
H1: Crochet stitch count checker

Everything above is arithmetic on one round, and arithmetic is the easy half. The half that actually costs people an evening is continuity: whether round 14 is worked across the number round 13 really finished with, all the way down a pattern. A round can be perfectly correct on its own and still be impossible, because the round above it did not leave the right number of stitches to work into.

That is why a pattern gets read end to end before it is trusted, one round against the next, with every stated count reconciled against the instructions that produce it. It is the job a technical editor does on a pattern before it is published, and it is not something a single text box can do for you.
